source: The descriptions of the skills that compete with this plugin's for the same requests: the released @joe-broadhead/opencode-linear, opencode-metaview, opencode-granola, opencode-plaud and opencode-notion packages, the github-* and slack-search skills, and the gws plugin.

skills.linear: Read before your first Linear tool call, linear_issues included. Use whenever the user asks about Linear or their Linear work - my issues, what I'm working on, what's in this cycle, a project's progress, an issue's comments, counts by state, a teammate's assignments - or names an identifier such as ENG-123 or a linear.app link. Covers choosing between linear_issues and list_issues, filters, paging, counts and citing links. Not for GitHub or Jira issues.
skills.github-code-research: Research code in a GitHub repository: find where something is defined, read files at a branch, tag or commit, compare versions, and follow the commit history to explain when and why code changed, citing permalinks. Use when the user asks how code in a GitHub repository works, where something is defined, what changed between versions or tags, or when and why it changed; not for files in the local checkout.
skills.github-issue-triage: Triage GitHub issues: list what is open or unlabelled, read issues, suggest labels from the repository's own and a priority, and find duplicates, open or closed, without changing anything unless asked. Use when the user asks what is open or unlabelled in a GitHub repository, to triage, sort or prioritise its issues, whether an issue is a duplicate, or to label, close or assign issues.
skills.github-pr-review: Review or summarise a GitHub pull request from its description, changed files, diff, earlier reviews and CI checks, and find out why CI failed, now or on an earlier run, without changing anything unless asked. Use when the user asks to review, summarise or check a GitHub pull request (a URL, OWNER/REPO#123 or a number), or why its CI or a check failed.
skills.slack-search: Use when the user wants to find, read, summarise or cite anything in their Slack (messages, threads, channels, people, canvases, lists or files), asks what was said or decided in Slack, wants to post, reply, draft or schedule a Slack message, or wants a script or cron job that reads Slack. Covers Slack's own tools in OpenCode, private-content consent, permalinks, and scripts through OpenCode's tools RPC instead of a Slack token or the Web API.
skills.metaview: Load before the first Metaview tool call (metaview_*, tools.metaview.*). For the user's recruiting interviews and candidates in Metaview - "what did <candidate> say about X", "summarise yesterday's screen with <name>", "which interviews did <interviewer> run last week", a candidate's interviews, including requests to guess a candidate's age, family or other personal traits, interview counts and themes by role, profiles and scorecards, reports, sourcing, screening, sequences and job posts, and Metaview sign-in. Not for non-hiring meetings (Granola), calendar scheduling or Slack.
skills.granola: Load before the first Granola tool call (granola_*, tools.granola.*). For questions about the user's Granola meetings: what was said, decided or assigned, notes, transcripts, follow-ups, questions across meetings, saving meetings as Markdown, or Granola sign-in and sign-out.
skills.opencode-plaud: Plaud voice recordings in OpenCode, to list, search and read recordings made with a Plaud device or app, with their transcripts, notes and highlights. Use when the user mentions Plaud, a voice recording or voice note, or something they recorded, such as "what did I record this week?" or "the action items from my last recording".
skills.opencode-gws: Use for any request about the user's Gmail, Google Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Tasks or other Google Workspace data, such as "check my inbox", "what's on my calendar", "find that doc", "send this email" or "share the file": how the gws_* tools find, read and change it (accounts, plan then approved commit, paging, errors). Use it instead of any gws-* CLI skill or a gws shell command, which skip the plugin's approvals.
skills.notion: Load before the first Notion tool call (notion_*, tools["notion"]). For the user's Notion workspace - a page, doc, spec, brief or wiki page, searching Notion for where something was written or decided, a database table such as a tracker, content calendar or project list, page comments and suggested edits, page history and backlinks, files on a page, Notion AI meeting notes, and Notion sign-in. Not for Google Docs, Drive, Gmail or Google Calendar (Google Workspace), Slack messages, GitHub code, Linear issues, or a recorded meeting (Granola or Wispr Flow).
skills.notion-write: Load before any Notion change - creating or editing a page or its properties, replacing page content, creating or changing a database, its properties or a view, adding, editing or resolving a comment or suggested edit, moving, duplicating or restoring a page, uploading a file or creating a folder, creating or updating a calendar event, or when the user asks to delete, restore a version, or hand work to a Notion agent.
skills.opencode-gws-recipes: Load before the first gws_read or gws_plan for an everyday Google Workspace task; it has the ready request: unread or recent mail and who sent it, mail in a time window, replies and drafts, the next meetings or a week's schedule, finding, summarising, sharing or trashing Drive files and Google Docs, reading or appending Sheets rows, and the standup, meeting-prep and weekly-digest reports. Prefer it to any gws-* CLI skill.
